requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely risks you may encounter while participating in sports and what you should do to anticipate, prevent, mitigate, and respond to those risks. (b) Show that you know first aid or understand the treatment for injuries that could occur while participating in sports, including sprains; strains; muscle cramps; contusions; abrasions; blisters; dehydration; heat reactions; fractures; injured teeth; head, neck, and back injuries; and concussions.

pamphlet_excerpts: Blisters Caused Continual: Blisters are usually caused by continual rubbing againstthe skin.
Friction Cause Hot: This friction will cause a hot spot, which signals thebeginning of a blister.
Blisters Feet Commonand: Blisters on the feet are the most commonand troublesome type.
Wear Properly Fittingshoes: So be sure that you wear properly fittingshoes and appropriate socks.
step_by_step_procedure: Feel Hot Spot: If you feel a hot spot developing, stop immediately and protect the tender area by applying anadhesive bandage or moleskin.
Blister Drained Wash: If a blister must be drained, first wash the blister with mildsoap and water.
Prickthe Edge Blister: Prickthe edge of the blister with a needle that has been sterilized in a flame.
Cover Itwith Adhesive: Cover itwith an adhesive bandage or other sterile dressing.

pamphlet_excerpts: Healthy Performer Sports: To be a strong, healthy performer in sports and in life, avoidtobacco, alcohol, and other harmful substances.
Tobacco Smoke Interferes: Tobacco smoke interferes with proper lung growth and function.
Coats Lungs Sticky: It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airwaysand air sacs of the lungs.
Athletes Their Lungs: Athletes need their lungs working atpeak capacity.
step_by_step_procedure: Usingtobacco Leave Gasping: Usingtobacco can leave you gasping for air when you need it most.
Tobacco-free Stamina: Being tobacco-free gives you the stamina to playsports.
Blood Carries Poisons: The blood carries the poisons from smoking to all parts of the body, from thebrain to the bladder.
Scientists Now Smoking: Scientists now know that smoking causescancers of the mouth, the larynx (voice box), the lungs, and thekidneys.

pamphlet_excerpts: Sportsmanship Means: Sometimes good sportsmanship means accepting whatmight be a poor decision made by an official, referee, orumpire.
Remember Struggling Sport: Remember, when you are struggling to be a good sport, that you have promised to exhibit the Scout spirit.
Showyour Spirit Cheerful: You showyour Scout spirit with a cheerful smile and living by the Scout Oath, which includes helping other people at all times.
Canbe Hard Sport: It canbe hard to be a good sport but you can always take pride in it.
step_by_step_procedure: Having Difficulty Officials: If you are having difficulty with the officials’ rulings, try to putyourself in their shoes.
Official Point View: From the official’s point of view, thedecision was consistent and fair.
Truly Disagree Officiating: If you truly disagree with the officiating after the game, it is acceptable to write a letter to the league commissioner orofficiating.
Considertaking Course: Also considertaking a course to qualify as an official.

requirements.lead_text: Select TWO of the following sports and discuss with your counselor how you will complete the requirements in 5(a) through 5(h) for each sport: badminton, baseball, basketball, bowling, cross-country, diving, field hockey, flag football, flag team, golf, gymnastics, ice hockey, lacrosse, soccer, softball, spirit/cheerleading, swimming, table tennis, tackle football, tennis, track and field, volleyball, water polo, and/or wrestling. Your counselor may approve in advance other recognized sports, but not any sport that is prohibited by Scouting America. The sports you choose must include regular practice sessions and at least four structured, officiated, scored games, meets, or contests against other competitive individuals or organized teams during the period of participation.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge related to a sport. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify how you might use skills and knowledge related to a sport to pursue a personal hobby and/or healthy lifestyle. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

step_by_step_procedure: Writing Down Training: By writing down your training, practice, and development, you will have the reward of looking back on how far you havecome and be able to set new.
Hardto Somewhere Life: It is hardto get somewhere in life without a written plan of where youare going and how you are going to get there.
Charts Own Charts: Fill in these charts or make your own charts byhand or using using a spreadsheet or other software tool.
Sportsmanship Means: Sometimes good sportsmanship means accepting whatmight be a poor decision made by an official, referee, orumpire.
